content.comment_body: Hello [product_name]-user, Today I’d like to share an interesting feature near the "comparator" block that might be quite useful for displaying values in text messages. I’ve tested this both in simulation and with real display modules from series [article_no] and [article_no]. Normally, analog block output values are limited to the range -32768 to 32767. When you reference a parameter of an analog block at runtime, the value is restricted at every analog block output. Even if an actual value is shown in a text message, that display value is limited accordingly. However, the "comparator" block, at least in my experience, behaves differently when used in text messages. It allows the display of actual values "Ax - Ay" in the wider range of -65536 to 65535. This seems to be unique to this context. ...If interested, check out the circuit examples attached. I’m curious to hear your thoughts on this. Best regards, [user_name]
That’s a great contribution from one of the top experts in this forum.
Hello, Did this information help you when programming the [product_name]? Do you have examples or any experimental results to share? Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, The special behavior of the "comparator" block can be used not only for textboxes—it’s also applicable in TIME-function blocks as a pointer, taking advantage of the larger value range (-65536 to 65535). Please review the attachment files to learn more about these possibilities. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user points out an undocumented aspect of the "comparator" block, showing that it supports a broader value range (-65536 to 65535) for display purposes compared to standard analog blocks (-32768 to 32767) in certain scenarios, such as text messages and TIME-function blocks. This uncovers inconsistencies in how value limitations are handled, which could affect users who expect uniform behavior and clarity in product features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate consistent value range treatment across all block types and prefer improved documentation to clearly explain any exceptions or special cases.
